description: The whole FILE classification corpus in one place, re-read from the recorded live transcripts rather than restated from memory. The account that produced them has since expired, so these are the recorded originals and each CONTENT_TYPE is quoted from the file it was measured on: .png image/png image, .jpg image/jpeg image, .gz application/gzip compressed, .zip application/zip compressed, .avi video/x-msvideo video (video AND audio at once), .mp3 audio/mpeg audio, .tsv text/tab-separated-values unknown (NOT a document), .txt text/plain document, and no extension application/octet-stream unknown. Each row travels the FULL path - real bytes on a stage, TO_FILE deriving a CONTENT_TYPE from the name, then the classifiers reading that derived field - so breaking EITHER lookup table, or the join between them, fails here. The .avi proves the category sets OVERLAP: FL_IS_x is NOT FL_GET_FILE_TYPE = 'x', and no refactor may implement one in terms of the other. The extension fixtures deliberately share one payload, so SIZE and ETAG are invariant across every name while CONTENT_TYPE varies with all of them, which is what lets the corpus blame the right table when a row moves. LAST_MODIFIED is asserted by SHAPE, never by value, because it is the fixture's own modification time. Converted from functions/file/FileCorpusTest; the Java staged its fixtures by writing bytes from Java, and the converted tests stage them in pure SQL with COPY INTO ... SINGLE = TRUE, which reproduces the Java's PAYLOAD byte for byte - 15 bytes with MD5 1e6e8ad188c5e661e4e146f5b7789e8a, the recorded PAYLOAD_ETAG. Two claims that need byte-level fixtures with no SQL surface stay in the trimmed Java class: the 69 raw PNG bytes with their recorded digest, and the zero-byte file.
